# Codex / Windmill assessment and Foo diagnosis

UTC assessment: 2026-10-28 08:42. No production mutations, inference tests, credentials, raw datasets, process environments, installations, or new schedules.

## Supported architecture

Keep the existing durable Foo Codex task as the coding and judgment owner; reuse existing Windmill deterministic SQL, checkpoint, provider and publisher jobs. Do not add an LLM manager or recursive orchestration. A native Windmill Codex job is supported conceptually through CLI/SDK/API, but is not currently deployed: the OffMenu MCP item listing returned no Codex script, flow or schedule. Existing platform health and verification schedules are present.

Official OpenAI documentation supports `codex exec` for scheduled pipelines, JSONL events and usage, schema-constrained outputs, explicit session-ID resume, and least-privilege sandboxing. Windmill documents AI sandbox scripts with persistent volumes, requiring object storage and nsjail. Its illustrative Codex skeleton uses outdated `codex --quiet` and shell interpolation: use current `codex exec` with separate argv instead, never blindly copy that skeleton.

Use gpt-6.1-sol with medium reasoning as the user-requested default when available; lower effort for simple bounded tasks, higher only for demonstrated hard reasoning. An explicit gpt-6.1 cloud create was reported unavailable by the parent. The successful diagnostic omitted model and selected medium; create did not return the saved model's resolved identity. Do not claim the exact resolved model.

Read-only Foo observation established Codex CLI 0.162.1 and `codex login status`: Logged in using ChatGPT. That proves installation and current local authentication method, not inference success, quota, worker-container credentials, API funds, or every model's availability. Restored consumer Codex usage does not imply separately billed Platform API entitlement. Official docs also support advanced ChatGPT-managed auth on trusted private automation runners; do not create or copy credentials merely to assess feasibility.

Persistent session state and credentials must be separate. Blindly syncing `.codex` to an object-storage volume risks syncing authentication material. Use explicit session IDs, isolated state/checkouts per lane, and one writer. Record compact task/commit/job/session references and token usage rather than repeatedly copying full histories.

MCP supports stdio and Streamable HTTP, but this conversation's connected tools do not prove that a Foo CLI process or Windmill worker has the same MCP configuration, authentication, permissions or reachability. Verify required tools fail closed before any native deployment. Current supported cloud task creation and messaging already provide durable ownership without new API credentials.

## Foo read-only measurement receipt

Single diagnostic task: `01a181a8-c114-77b2-b98e-030c3a46c008`.
Initial turn: `01a181a8-cbcb-7351-bb52-89925f4af3d6`, completed. Remote: `fragrant-tree-12463214`, connected and authorized. No old utility owner was resumed. A timing-race follow-up message requested the result while read status lagged; its turn `01a181ac-7f3c-77f4-b7be-3966284450b8` restated existing evidence and explicitly stopped, with no new measurement reported.

Host verified `foo`, 08:38:18Z. Ten vmstat intervals beginning about 08:38:33Z showed CPU idle 91–93%, I/O wait 5–6%, runnable 0–1, blocked 1–3, swap-out zero throughout. Independent 10.000884-second counters at 08:39:56.419652Z: pswpin 582657 to 582661 (16,384 bytes); pswpout 4230969 unchanged. Swap occupied 8,350,804 of 8,388,604 KiB. This is not evidence of active swap thrashing.

Two five-second iostat intervals, excluding boot average:

| Device | Read KiB/s | Write KiB/s | Read await ms | Write await ms | Queue | Util % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dm-0 first | 11,032.8 | 141,508.0 | 2.05 | 8.86 | 150.28 | 92.40 |
| dm-0 second | 12,312.8 | 143,106.4 | 1.78 | 8.43 | 149.61 | 91.08 |
| nvme0n1 first | 5,551.2 | 69,974.4 | 3.72 | 17.37 | 147.20 | 89.22 |
| nvme0n1 second | 6,068.8 | 70,853.6 | 3.17 | 16.15 | 143.85 | 88.26 |
| nvme1n1 first | 5,481.6 | 71,544.0 | 0.23 | 1.68 | 14.91 | 22.86 |
| nvme1n1 second | 6,244.0 | 72,933.6 | 0.26 | 1.83 | 16.95 | 22.98 |

PID 377989 maps to assessor016 `corpus-global-qualification-cache-headroom-016-20261028`, `qualifier_job_adapter.py`. It remained D-state, with waits `md_flush_request` to `jbd2_log_wait_commit`; 10-second read/write deltas 16,564,224 / 692,224 bytes.

PID 380537 maps to bulkSQL003 `north-star-full-bulk-003`, `derive_north_star_bulk.py`. It remained D-state, with waits `rq_qos_wait` to `folio_wait_bit_common`; deltas 3,698,688 / 229,961,728 bytes. Aggregate device writes exceed these processes' measured writes; do not attribute all traffic to them.

At 08:41:17Z the related trees contained six processes: three sleeping, three in disk sleep, none runnable. Declared 64 qualification workers were not 64 currently ready CPU workers. Both operational receipts were running. NorthStar phase metadata was stale (08:19:17Z), with 9,797/9,797 assets, building-consumer-index, complete false; not completion proof.

At 08:40:54.786947Z: CPU reservation 20,000 millicores of 27,000 admission budget; RAM available 46,248,009,728 bytes, declarations 27,514,634,240 bytes, leaving 10,143,440,896 after 8 GiB reserve. Filesystem free 110,687,260,672 bytes, about 95% used. Existing output reservations 38,712,352,206 bytes plus 70 GiB reserve and 128 MiB bookkeeping require 114,008,497,614 bytes: already short 3,321,236,942 bytes. National 4 GiB requires 118,303,464,910 bytes; basis 10 GiB requires 124,745,915,854 bytes; both require 129,040,883,150 bytes. Neither has an active reservation.

At 08:41:17Z PSI avg10: CPU some 0.00%; memory some/full 0.07%; I/O some 17.06%, full 16.12%.

Conclusion: current bottleneck is disk/commit latency and disk admission headroom, not CPU or active swap thrashing. Keep national and basis withheld. Let current work drain and let its existing owner perform normal verified reservation reconciliation; reassess admission afterward. More workers do not solve these waits. Investigate persistent NVMe latency imbalance without destructive changes. Parent retains ongoing production ownership; this diagnostic is finished.

# Read-only topology follow-through

Task: `01a181a8-c114-77b2-b98e-030c3a46c008`; turn: `01a181af-7049-75c7-8f0a-2cc9c5954c61`, completed.

Read-only follow-through on `foo` at **2026-10-28T08:45:32Z** found no confirmed device fault or configuration difference explaining the latency imbalance.

- **Topology:** output filesystem → ext4 → `dm-0` (`ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv`) → `md126p3` → `md126`, **two-device RAID0, 128 KiB chunks**, spanning `nvme0n1` and `nvme1n1`. Array state: `clean`. A slower member can constrain this shared filesystem.
- **Both devices:** Kingston `SFYRSK1000G`, firmware `EIFK31.6`, controller state `live`, PCIe **16 GT/s ×4**, matching maximum link capability. Identical scheduler `none`, queue request limit **1023**, **19 controller queues**, write-back cache and **2,000 µs** writeback-latency setting.
- **Temperatures:** `nvme0` composite **58.85°C**, sensor 2 **77.85°C**; `nvme1` composite **53.85°C**, sensor 2 **78.85°C**. Both composite alarms **0**, warning threshold **83.85°C**, critical **88.85°C**. These readings do **not establish thermal throttling**.
- Available PCIe AER correctable, nonfatal and fatal counters were **all zero** on both controllers.

**Limitations:** `nvme smart-log` could not run because `/dev/nvme0` and `/dev/nvme1` are absent from this execution environment. Consequently, media errors, wear, spare capacity and thermal-throttling history remain unverified. Sensor-2 maximum-temperature attributes returned `Input/output error` on both devices; that attribute failure alone does not establish a storage fault. No elevated access was requested.

**Conclusion:** the measured latency asymmetry remains unexplained. Safe next step for the existing host/storage owner: obtain read-only NVMe SMART/error logs and thermal-transition counters through their established host access, and compare cooling and device wear before considering changes. No changes, benchmarks, self-tests or workload actions performed; stopped.
